All those fat asses who refuse to take care of their bodies because they think they are living a curious life, which is definitely compatible with a healthy life, are not reading books, going on nature walks, making art or writing poems during the time they are not at the gym. They're sitting in front of the TV, binge watching Netflix and ordering pizza. They're combing Tumblr for bias confirmation that their FUPA is totally hot. By not exercising they may actually be getting stupider.

When we engage in vigorous exercise we experience neurogenesis - the creation of new cells. Exercise literally creates new brain cells that become permanent when we use them. One of the best ways to really have a life fueled by curiosity is to workout several times a week while engaging in positive mental activities. Exercise increases blood flow to the brain and encourages focus and concentration. And if that isn't enough to persuade a sane person, the hippocampus, the part of the brain responsible for learning and memory, is activated and regular exercise can prevent the hippocampus shrinkage that occurs in old age. Exercise also has a direct affect on hyperactivity and attention deficit disorders. People who exercise regularly reduce their chances of developing dementia, even those with a genetic predisposition for conditions like Alzheimers.

You want a curious life? Exercise.

Also, there's the fact that exercise is a whole world of deep activities to learn about, think about, and be curious about. Sports are deep, and to some extent they are intellectual and artistic, just like fatty's precious drawings or whatever. Even weightlifting is interesting and deep; it encourages and sometimes requires thought about mechanics, physiology, nutrition, medicine, psychology, and so on. It's not just lifting things and putting them down again. You have to do that efficiently enough to make progress, and you have to manage your own tendency to want to avoid doing it (supposing you have one), and you have to do it all without hurting yourself too much. You have to choose which parts of your body to sculpt, what goal to aim for in sculpting them, and what technique to use to achieve that goal. Like everything, it seems to become more complicated as you look at it more closely, Like anything, it's as intellectual and creative as you want to make it. It can easily be less "boring" than some fool's cruddy amateur paintings.
